existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicinalProductContraindication` is removed as an R6 resource and its content must be transformed into `ClinicalUseDefinition` with contraindication-specific structure. The top migration concerns are resource identity, mandatory/type-changed `subject`, moved/renamed contraindication fields, and population/indication representation changes. Confidence is high for computable differences, with residual uncertainty about the official design rationale and preferred cross-version maps.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: The change is a consolidation and remodel rather than a field-by-field compatible evolution. R4 top-level contraindication fields generally move under `ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication`, several names change, CodeableConcept fields become CodeableReference fields, and R6 introduces discriminator constraints around `type`. Down-conversion from R6 to R4 is lossy for new targets, concept/reference alternatives, modifier status, group-based populations, library/applicability logic, and management/category metadata.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the R4 resource is not present in R6 and that `ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication` is the relevant successor, based on local package indexes, `fhir-old-types`, and the R6 StructureDefinition. Confidence is medium for exact business-safe transforms because no official diff, ConceptMap, or narrative migration guidance was available.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
MedicinalProductContraindication has a resource-identity break: R4 MedicinalProductContraindication resource is removed and replaced by ClinicalUseDefinition. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 97/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.

topFindings.title: R4 MedicinalProductContraindication resource is removed and replaced by ClinicalUseDefinition
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: the resource type, StructureDefinition URL, generated model, server surface, and reference target name change; raw R4 instances are also old-valid/new-invalid because the R4 `resourceType` is not an R6 resource.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: otherTherapy child names and medication representation change
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 child names and choice-element names are not valid R6 child names; runtime/API/codegen also changes generated accessors and target-resource handling.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: population changes from inline Population datatype to Reference(Group)
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an inline R4 `Population` object is not a valid R6 `Reference(Group)`; R6-to-R4 loss occurs unless the referenced Group can be dereferenced and expressed in the old Population datatype.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: therapeuticIndication Reference is replaced by inline contraindication.indication content
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `Reference(MedicinalProductIndication)` is not valid at an R6 inline backbone location; R6-to-R4 loss also occurs when inline indication content has no stable resource identity to reference.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Top-level contraindication details move under ClinicalUseDefinition.contraindication with renamed paths
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4-shaped top-level fields such as `disease` or `otherTherapy` are not valid R6 fields on `ClinicalUseDefinition`; runtime/API/codegen paths also change.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 requires a type discriminator and contraindication branch consistency
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a migrated R6-shaped instance with contraindication content but no `type`, or with the wrong type code, fails R6 validation.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Subject becomes mandatory and changes from Reference to CodeableReference with different targets
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances that omit `subject` cannot validate after migration without adding one; runtime/API/codegen also changes because references are nested under `CodeableReference.reference`.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Disease, diseaseStatus, and comorbidity change from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: after the path move, placing a raw `CodeableConcept` directly where R6 expects a `CodeableReference` is invalid; R6-to-R4 loss occurs when the R6 value uses `.reference` rather than `.concept`.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 adds modifier status with no R4 counterpart
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: optional R6 status can carry lifecycle semantics that R4 has no local field to preserve; no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break is introduced by this optional element.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 adds optional ClinicalUseDefinition metadata and logic elements not representable in R4
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: optional R6-only metadata and logic have no standard local R4 destination; no old-valid/new-invalid forward break is introduced.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
